census.origin: Queen Anne's County was created in 1706 (Chapter 3, Acts of 1706). The County was named for Queen Anne (1665-1714), who ruled Great Britain and Ireland from 1702 to 1714. During Queen Anne's reign, Maryland was governed as a royal colony rather than as a proprietary province.

council_members.name: Ashley H. Kaiser, Esq.
council_members.title: Council President
council_members.bio: Ashley lives in the Providence Farms community with her husband and two sons. She is an attorney and non-profit professional with experience in advocacy at all levels of government. Ashley is a graduate of Queen Anne's County High School with a passion for preserving the quality of life in our community.

council_members.name: Daniel B. Worth
council_members.title: Council Member
council_members.bio: Dan grew up in Dundalk, a suburb of Baltimore. He attended Drexel University where he received a degree in Electrical Engineering in 1980. He moved to Centreville to start a family in 1998 and has three daughters. In 2017, he retired from NASA and began working part-time as a contractor at NASA.

council_members.name: Sandy L. Huffer
council_members.title: Council Member
council_members.bio: Sandy grew up in Centreville where she developed her love for the Eastern Shore. Graduated from The University of Delaware with a Bachelor's degree majoring in Accounting. Retired in 2021 as Director of Financial Operations at Anne Arundel Medical Center in Annapolis. She and her partner restored and reside at one of the Captains Houses in Centreville on Corsica Creek which is on the National Register of Historic Places.

top_issues.significance: Infrastructure development and capacity issues are crucial for Queen Anne's County as they directly impact growth, transportation, and public services. The county is experiencing growth pressures and needs to manage infrastructure to accommodate new developments while maintaining quality of life for residents.
top_issues.recent_developments: Recent developments include the consideration of a moratorium on new growth due to sewer capacity issues (2025-08-28), discussions on connecting county trails (2024-10-08), and the state plan to replace the Chesapeake Bay Bridge with two new spans (2024-11-12). The county is also upgrading wastewater handling in Centreville (2024-04-12).

top_issues.significance: Development and zoning regulations are significant for Queen Anne's County as they influence how land is used, affecting both economic development and quality of life. The county needs to balance growth with preserving its character and environment.
top_issues.recent_developments: Recent developments include the regulation of short-term rentals (2024-11-01, 2024-12-11), discussions on cannabis expansion (2025-01-29), and proposals for new developments such as the Chesapeake Beach Club Hotel (2024-12-27) and infill affordable housing in Grasonville (2024-12-26). Residents have protested certain developments, like the planned Royal Farms development (2025-04-19).

top_issues.significance: Budget and financial management are critical for Queen Anne's County as they determine the county's ability to fund public services and infrastructure. The county faces challenges related to cost shifts from the state and potential service cuts due to tax breaks.
top_issues.recent_developments: Recent developments include the proposed FY25 budget (2024-04-05), discussions on cost shifts from the state to counties (2025-03-01), and concerns about the impact of proposed tax breaks on lower-income counties (2025-03-06). The county has also approved the Chesapeake College budget request (2025-04-19).

# Queen Anne's County FY2026 Budget Analysis

## Executive Summary

Queen Anne's County approved a $209 million budget for fiscal year 2026 (beginning July 1, 2025), representing an 8.2% increase from the FY2025 revised budget of $193.1 million. The budget maintains all existing tax rates while significantly increasing funding for education and public safety.
